extra.message: The 'remoteUrl' request parameter (set at InitializationFilter.java:818 from httpRequest.getParameter("remoteUrl")) is passed into StartupFilter.renderTemplate() (StartupFilter.java:266-280), which copies every model field into the Velocity context via reflection with no escaping, then rendered here as ${remoteUrl} inside an HTML attribute with no $esc/EscapeTool usage anywhere in this filter. A value like "><script>alert(1)</script> breaks out of the attribute and executes during the pre-authentication install wizard flow.

The 'username' request parameter (InitializationFilter.java:827: wizardModel.remoteUsername = httpRequest.getParameter("username")) is reflected unescaped as ${remoteUsername} in this HTML attribute via the same unescaped Velocity reflection mechanism in StartupFilter.renderTemplate(). Exploitable pre-authentication during the install wizard.

The 'database_connection' request parameter (InitializationFilter.java:589: wizardModel.databaseConnection = httpRequest.getParameter("database_connection")) is reflected unescaped as ${databaseConnection} via the same unescaped Velocity reflection path in StartupFilter.renderTemplate(). The identical unescaped pattern repeats for databaseDriver (line 30), databaseName (lines 54, 78), createDatabaseUsername (line 89) and createDatabasePassword (line 99) in this same file, all sourced directly from request parameters in InitializationFilter.java, all reachable pre-authentication during the install wizard.

InitializationFilter.java:873 does errors.put("install.testing.invalidProductionUrl", new Object[]{ wizardModel.remoteUrl }) with the raw, attacker-supplied 'remoteUrl' request parameter. This template renders it via $l10n.get($error.getKey()).insert($error.getValue()) directly into the

element's HTML body with no escaping, worse than an attribute-context issue since no quote-breakout is even needed. Reachable pre-authentication via the install wizard's remote-testing step.

'remoteUrl' is taken directly from httpRequest.getParameter("remoteUrl") (line 818) with no host/scheme allowlist, then passed to TestInstallUtil.testConnection(wizardModel.remoteUrl) which opens an HttpURLConnection to the attacker-supplied URL (TestInstallUtil.java:224-239: new URL(urlString).openConnection(); urlConnect.getContent()). This runs in the pre-authentication install wizard, so any network attacker who reaches a not-yet-configured OpenMRS instance can force it to make arbitrary outbound HTTP requests (e.g. to internal/cloud-metadata hosts), a classic SSRF primitive.

TestInstallUtil.getResourceInputStream() is called with the attacker-controlled wizardModel.remoteUrl plus the username/password the installer just typed in (wizardModel.remoteUsername, wizardModel.remotePassword). getResourceInputStream/createConnection (TestInstallUtil.java:249-274) opens an HttpURLConnection to that URL and POSTs the Base64-encoded credentials to it. Because remoteUrl is attacker-supplied and unvalidated, an attacker who reaches the pre-auth install wizard can redirect this POST to a server they control and capture the installer's credentials.

A bare 'new XStreamMarshaller()' (lines 184-186) is wrapped in a MarshallingHttpMessageConverter (lines 188-193) and registered globally in Spring MVC's HttpMessageConverter list (line 163), with the "xml" extension mapped to APPLICATION_XML in configureContentNegotiation(). Unlike org.openmrs.serialization.SimpleXStreamSerializer, which explicitly calls setupXStreamSecurity() to constrain allowed types, this XStreamMarshaller has no type allowlist/denylist configured at all. Any @RequestBody controller (in core or an installed module) that accepts this converter's output would unmarshal attacker-supplied XML using XStream's default reflection-based converters, which is a well-known vector for instantiating arbitrary types from XML and achieving deserialization gadget chains / RCE.

setupXStreamSecurity() only additively permits types via allowTypes()/allowTypesByWildcard()/allowTypeHierarchy() based on admin-configured global-property whitelist entries; it never calls XStream.setupDefaultSecurity(xstream) or xstream.addPermission(NoTypePermission.NONE) to establish a deny-by-default baseline first. XStream therefore falls back to only its built-in denylist of previously-disclosed gadget classes, not a true allowlist, so unknown/future deserialization gadgets are not blocked. HibernateSerializedObjectDAO deserializes SerializedObject rows from the database through this serializer.

simpleMappingExceptionResolver() maps java.lang.Exception to the view name "uncaughtException", but no uncaughtException.jsp (or equivalent view) exists anywhere under webapp/src/main/webapp, and webapp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml defines no <error-page> element. Any unhandled exception thrown while processing a request therefore fails to resolve a view and propagates to the servlet container's default error handling, which typically renders the full exception class, message and stack trace (including internal file/package paths) to the client triggering it.

extra.message: On a SQLException during the install wizard's DB-setup SQL execution, the raw SQL text and the JDBC driver's exception message are concatenated into an error string shown back to the browser ("Error executing sql: " + sql + " - " + sqlex.getMessage()), disclosing internal SQL/schema/driver details to whoever is interacting with the pre-authentication install wizard.

extra.message: The <session-config><cookie-config> block sets <http-only>true</http-only> but never sets <secure>true</secure>. Without the Secure attribute, the JSESSIONID session cookie can be transmitted over plain HTTP, allowing it to be captured by a network attacker (e.g. via SSL-stripping or a mixed-content HTTP endpoint) even when the application is primarily served over HTTPS.
